newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Hub Power drops 3.40 percent.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Hub Power drops 3.40 percent.

text.p: Hub Power Co Ltd fell 1.35 rupees, or 3.40 percent, to 38.15 on Thursday on news the government plans to renegotiate agreements with private power companies for the purchase of electricty, dealers said.
Turnover of over 7.7 million Hub Power shares was recorded in early trade at the Karachi Stock Exchange.
"The news has jolted the market because the earnings of private power projects will come down if agreements are re-negotiated," dealer Shakil Anwar said.

Pakistan's Federal Minister for Water and Power, Nisar Ali, said in Islamabad on Wednesday the government would re-negotiate tariff agreements with the sponsors of private sector thermal power projects as the electricity purchasing rates were high.
"We cannot pass on this electricity to the consumers at such high prices," daily Business Recorder quoted Nisar Ali as saying. "The price of 6.5 cents per unit is not acceptable to us."
Ali's statement triggered selling of energy stocks and weakened the overall sentiment at the Karachi bourse, dealers said.
"Investors are jittery and lack confidence regarding consistency in government policies," Anwar said.
Another dealer, Hina Akhlaq, said a revision of power tariffs was possible as state-run power companies faced financial problems and one had already defaulted on payments to the Hub Power.
"But if agreements are revised, it would damage Pakistan's image and shake the confidence of foreign and local investors."
Anwar said the entire energy sector has been hit by the news and analyst see sharp falls in the earnings of private power companies if the government goes ahead with its plan.
